name: Hypo-Haus
elevationDatum: Rigid local foundation y=0; real metres +X east, +Y up, +Z south. Two mapped controls fix rotation, baked into the geometry once. No terrain or Mercator stretch.
note: HVB Tower’s three pointed suspended prisms are carried by unequal silver cylindrical pylons and their large 40–50 m collar brackets, with a central glazed web and a distinct staggered skyline. The highest published 113.7 m replaces rounded OSM 114 m; other part heights follow OSM and are not a new survey. The official description counts four main pylons; the mapped 110 m small adjoining service drum is retained as an auxiliary part, not a fifth independent main pylon. The tall prism lacks min_height in OSM; its 17 m soffit is estimated consistently with the other suspended prisms and exterior photographs. Circular centres/radii are fitted to mapped rings. Fine aluminium seams, facade cadence and central-web glazing are simplified. The modernized tower is the scope; lower surrounding campus, landscaping and signage are excluded. The June 2008 photo initially returned by the article dossier was excluded from current facade evidence; both retained exterior references are from June 2017, after the tower renovation. Cityscape: not tested; Full 3D world: not tested.
